question: What is the primary purpose of a sample design in research?

options.A: To eliminate the need for data collection entirely
options.B: To select a representative group from a larger population
options.C: To study every single member of the target population
options.D: To increase the total cost of the research project

explanation: A sample design provides a structured plan to choose a subset that accurately reflects the wider population. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h1)

question: Why is studying an entire population usually impractical for nursing studies?

options.A: Ethics committees strictly forbid studying large groups
options.B: Target populations never have enough members to study
options.C: Research findings become less accurate with more participants
options.D: Resource limitations like time and money make it impossible

explanation: High costs, vast geographical areas, and time constraints prevent researchers from reaching every individual in a large population. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h1)

question: What does a sampling frame represent in a research study?

options.A: The physical list used to select study participants
options.B: The statistical formula used to calculate sample size
options.C: The final group of patients who complete the study
options.D: The theoretical group of all people with a condition

explanation: The sampling frame is the concrete list or database containing members of the population from which the sample is drawn. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h2)

question: A researcher wants to study nurses in a specific teaching hospital and obtains the official payroll register. What is this payroll register?
explanation: The payroll register serves as the accessible list of population members used for drawing the actual sample. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h2)

question: Which sampling method gives every population member an equal and independent chance of selection?
explanation: Simple random sampling ensures every individual has an equal probability of being chosen without bias. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h3)

question: When should a researcher choose stratified random sampling over simple random sampling?

options.A: To completely eliminate all forms of random sampling error
options.B: To ensure adequate representation of specific minority subgroups
options.C: When the research budget is extremely limited and small
options.D: When there is no available list of the target population

explanation: Stratification divides the population into groups to guarantee that smaller subgroups are properly represented in the final sample. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h3)

question: What is the main characteristic of non-probability sampling methods?

options.A: Every person in the population has an equal chance of selection
options.B: Sampling error can be measured with exact mathematical precision
options.C: Participant selection depends on the researcher's judgment
options.D: Findings can always be generalized to the global population

explanation: Non-probability methods use subjective techniques rather than random chance to select study participants. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h4)

question: A nurse researcher studies recovering drug addicts who introduce their peers to the study. Which sampling method is this?
explanation: Snowball sampling relies on initial participants to refer other eligible individuals, ideal for hidden or hard-to-reach groups. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h4)

question: What does statistical power mean in a research study?

options.A: The ability of a study to detect a real effect or difference
options.B: The probability of making a false positive statistical error
options.C: The financial budget allocated for participant recruitment
options.D: The total number of patients enrolled in the sampling frame

explanation: Statistical power is the probability that a study will correctly detect a real effect when one exists. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h5)

question: Why do researchers factor patient drop-out rates into their initial sample size calculation?

options.A: To increase the total cost estimates submitted to the ethics board
options.B: To eliminate the need for random sampling techniques
options.C: To comply with ethical guidelines regarding patient payment
options.D: To ensure enough data remains for analysis despite participant attrition

explanation: Anticipating dropouts allows researchers to recruit extra participants so the final analyzed sample remains statistically adequate. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h5)

question: What is the difference between sampling error and sampling bias?

options.A: Sampling error only happens in qualitative nursing research studies
options.B: Sampling error is natural variation, while bias is systematic distortion
options.C: Sampling bias is caused entirely by poor sample size calculations
options.D: Sampling bias can never be prevented, while error can be avoided

explanation: Sampling error stems from natural chance differences, whereas sampling bias comes from flawed selection procedures. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h6)

question: Which scenario is a classic example of sampling bias in a hospital study?

options.A: Calculating a larger sample size to account for potential patient dropouts
options.B: Using a table of random numbers to select clinic files from a registry
options.C: Surveying only patients who visit the private VIP ward about hospital costs
options.D: Selecting every tenth patient from a complete inpatient admission list

explanation: Focusing on a single privileged group skews the data and fails to represent the general hospital population accurately. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h6)

question: What is required before any patient is enrolled in a research sample?
explanation: Informed consent ensures that participants understand the study and choose to join completely free from coercion. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h7)

question: Why is recruiting patients from one's own clinical ward considered an ethical challenge for nurse researchers?

options.A: Patients on clinical wards are completely incapable of understanding research
options.B: Informed consent is legally unnecessary when nurses treat their own patients
options.C: Patients might feel pressured to participate due to their dependent relationship
options.D: Hospital management will automatically reject any clinical study involving staff

explanation: Patients may fear that refusing to participate could negatively affect their ongoing nursing care and clinical treatment. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h7)
